behavior.consumer_hit: returned second == 0: the fresh 0x58-byte node is sized-deleted and the existing node (returned first) is returned
behavior.consumer_insert: otherwise insert_and_rebalance is called with (insert_left, fresh node, returned second as parent, header), the count at container +0x28 is incremented, and the fresh node is returned
behavior.empty_tree: hint == header and root null: the full walk returns (0, header)
behavior.end_hint_above_rightmost: hint == header, count non-zero and sought key > rightmost key: (0, rightmost)
behavior.end_hint_other: hint == header otherwise: the full unique-position walk below
behavior.fallback: when the hint adjacency check fails (predecessor key >= sought, or successor key <= sought), the function tail-jumps to the twin full search at 0x514b220 with (container, sought key) and returns its result
behavior.general: insert-hint unique position: given a container, a hint node and a signed int32 key, return the (first, second) pair the two insert consumers feed to _Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance: (node, 0) on an exact hit, otherwise an insertion position (first, second) as detailed per arm
behavior.hint_equal: hint key == sought key: (hint, 0) exact hit
behavior.hint_leftmost_below: hint == leftmost and sought key < hint key: (hint, hint)
behavior.insert_left_rule: insert_left = 1 when returned first is non-null, else 1 when returned second == header, else (sought key < [returned second + 0x20])
behavior.pred_adjacent_no_right_child: predecessor key < sought key and the predecessor has a null right child: (0, predecessor)
behavior.pred_adjacent_right_child: predecessor key < sought key and the predecessor has a non-null right child: (hint, hint)
behavior.succ_adjacent_no_right_child: successor key > sought key and the hint has a null right child: (0, hint)
behavior.succ_adjacent_right_child: successor key > sought key and the hint has a non-null right child: (successor, successor)
behavior.walk_hit: full walk ends at a node whose key equals the sought key: (node, 0)
behavior.walk_miss_left: full walk ends going left at a node whose key is greater than the sought key: (0, that node) unless it is the leftmost, in which case the predecessor step is skipped and the same pair is returned; otherwise the predecessor is stepped to and the hit/miss rule is applied to (predecessor, that node)
behavior.walk_miss_right: full walk ends going right at a node whose key is less than the sought key: (0, that node)
behavior.walk_rule: from the root, go left when sought key < node key, else right, until the next child is null; the last visited node decides the result per the hit/miss rules above
